component.name: Salvajocs
component.summary: Back up and restore game saves

description.p: Back up and restore game saves in a restic-format repository. A save backed up from a Wine or Proton prefix on Linux restores on native Windows, and the other way round.

It finds saves with the ludusavi game manifest, in native folders, Steam Proton prefixes, the Heroic, Lutris and Bottles prefixes on Linux, and Wine prefixes you configure. It also backs up registry keys. The repository can be a local folder, a REST server, an rclone remote or an OpenDAL service, and you can read it with the restic command line.

description.p: Updates install only when signed with the salvajocs release key. A custom game written by another PC is used here only after you accept it in Custom games; Not now sets it aside and you can still use it later. Only one salvajocs runs at a time, Escape closes dialogs that can be cancelled, and the REST password is kept in the keyring. Many restore and backup fixes, among them AppData folders spelled with another case.
The Restore tab's list of games scrolls when it is longer than the window, also while a job runs.

Only Back up writes custom games and the Old backups rules to the repository. Opening the app and the new Read repository button only read them, and custom games can be edited without the repository. When a game or the rules changed here and on another PC, Back up shows both versions and you choose which one to keep.

Custom games are stored in the repository, so every PC that uses it has the same ones. A changed file on the Backup tab and in the restore plan has a Details button that shows what differs, such as line endings. The restore plan has a checkbox on each file and registry key, to restore only some. The Backup and Restore tabs sort their games by name, last backup or space used, and Settings shows the version and build.

The AppImage updates itself. The Backup tab compares saves across Linux and Windows through the folder pairs, with Choose folders… for games it cannot match, and scrolls without lag. A backup remembers the Wine prefix it came from, and a restore fills it in again. The single-game restore plan is a file tree. The manifest status, the update notice and Back up share one bar at the bottom.

Restore several games in one go. The Restore tab shows the plan as soon as a snapshot is chosen, without downloading it first. The Backup tab shows icons for the files that are new, changed or removed since the newest backup, and skips games whose saves equal it. A System, Light or Dark theme switch in Settings. A remembered server password is no longer removed by Settings.

When the repository is missing, the app says what to do and opens Settings. Creating a repository asks on its own screen, with the compression level. Folders that hold only one folder show on one line in the Backup tab. The AppImage process is named salvajocs.

Choose which files, folders and registry keys of each game are backed up, and which old backups to keep. Delete backups from the Restore tab. On Linux, the scan finds the Wine prefixes of Heroic, Lutris and Bottles, and shows its progress. The app draws its own title bar. Custom game files have a Linux and a Windows path; files of custom games from 0.3.x must be added again.

The app is called Salvajocs. On Wayland, the task bar and title bar show the app icon when an AppImage tool installed the app under another name. Support for running inside a Flatpak sandbox is removed.

Each storage backend has its own named fields and a help link to its docs page. Other options are under Advanced options. Rclone remotes show in a list. The repository password is now called the encryption password. Compression is a dropdown with presets and a custom level.

A new look: green light and dark themes, a more readable font, icons, and a save bar on the Backup tab. Restore lists the games in a sidebar. Labels and messages are plainer, and keyboard and screen reader order follows the screen.
